Goal: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

Required evaluation protocol: Shared evaluation protocol (from limitation group C: G2, G10, G12, G16): checkpoints and hyper-parameters are selected on a held-out validation split of the SOURCE modalities and never on the target test set, and the MVFA baseline is re-run under the same rule; results are reported under a modality-disjoint leave-one-modality-out split (RESC and OCT17 are held out together, never one with the other in training), with patient-level separation where identifiers exist, over at least 3 random seeds and 3 few-shot support draws with mean and standard deviation, and against the missing baselines named in G12 where relevant.
Inspiration (use analogy, not replication): TITLE: Occlusion attribution of MVFA's detection branch as pseudo-masks for its segmentation branch
SUMMARY: Train the detection branch on image-level labels, then mark as anomalous the patches whose replacement by their nearest normal-bank feature most reduces the detection branch's image score, and use these attribution maps as segmentation targets.
HYPOTHESIS: Occlusion-attribution pseudo-masks from the image-label-trained detection branch achieve at least 8 points higher Dice against true masks than nearest-neighbour pseudo-masks on at least two of the three masked datasets, and MVFA trained on them recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC.
RATIONALE: The veto idea uses the detection branch's map as a second opinion. By analogy with counterfactual explanation in weakly supervised localisation, the detection branch, trained with reliable image labels on all six datasets, implicitly knows which patches make an image abnormal: replacing such a patch by its closest normal counterpart should lower the image score. This counterfactual occlusion gives a causal attribution rather than a correlational map, uses only components that MVFA already has (det_adapters and a normal bank), and directly targets the problem's question of what image-level labels can teach the segmentation branch.
METHOD: 1) Stage 1: train det_adapters only (train_zero.py, seg loss off) on all six sources, 20 epochs, selected on source-validation image AUROC. 2) For each abnormal source image: features F per level; for each patch p, F_p' = F with patch p replaced by its nearest neighbour in the dataset's normal bank at each level; attribution a_p = score(F) - score(F_p') with score the det branch's mean-pooled anomaly output (batched over patches: 289 forward passes of the adapters only, CLIP features cached). 3) Pseudo-mask = a_p > 99th percentile of a on normal source-validation images (where attributions should be small). 4) Stage 2: train seg branch on these masks with Focal + Dice; det branch continues. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; NN pseudo-masks; occlusion pseudo-masks; Grad-CAM of the det branch (cheaper attribution baseline). Metrics: pseudo-mask Dice, trained pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC. Falsified if occlusion masks do not beat NN pseudo-masks by 8 Dice points on two masked datasets or do not beat Grad-CAM.
